question: Why is catching maternal distress early so important for a mum in labour?

options.A: It guarantees the avoidance of a Caesarean section
options.B: It prevents prolonged exhaustion and stalled labour progress
options.C: It stops the production of amniotic fluid completely
options.D: It eliminates the need for any pain relief medication

explanation: Great job! Catching distress early breaks the cycle of stress hormones, helping her contractions stay strong and keeping her labour moving forward. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T002#GNS226_U4_T002_h1)

question: How often should a nurse check a stable HIV patient's weight to catch any nutritional drops early?

options.A: At every clinic visit
options.B: Once every five years
options.C: Only after surgery
options.D: Only when they have a fever

explanation: You got it! Checking weight regularly helps you spot trouble before it turns into severe malnutrition or muscle wasting. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T5#GNS216_U6_T5_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of maintaining the cold chain in immunization programs?

options.A: To ensure vaccine potency and effectiveness
options.B: To reduce the manufacturing cost of the vials
options.C: To prevent theft of medical supplies from the clinic
options.D: To freeze the vaccines into solid blocks for easy transport

explanation: The cold chain keeps vaccines at the correct low temperature so they do not spoil and lose their potency. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T7#GNS124_U2_T7_h5)

question: What kind of material is mainly examined in qualitative data analysis?

options.A: Large spreadsheets of blood pressure numbers
options.B: Words, interview transcripts, and observations
options.C: Hospital financial ledgers and purchase orders
options.D: Laboratory test tube measurements and weights

explanation: While quantitative deals with numbers, qualitative research is all about stories, spoken words, and human experiences. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T16#GNS217_U3_T16_h5)

question: What happens to the marks on daily tally sheets at the end of a clinic day?

options.A: The marks are counted and transferred into monthly summary registers
options.B: The tally marks are erased so the sheet can be reused tomorrow
options.C: The papers are burned to protect patient confidentiality
options.D: The sheets are mailed directly to the international health organization

explanation: Spot on! At the end of the day, we count up the tally marks so they can feed into our bigger monthly summary books and reports. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T13#GNS225_U2_T13_h4)

question: When is a nurse most likely to use the rectal route of medication administration?

options.A: When the patient has severe vomiting and cannot swallow pills
options.B: When the patient prefers taking sweet liquids over tablets
options.C: When the drug is only available in a chewable tablet form
options.D: When the patient needs a slow-release oral multivitamin

explanation: Vomiting prevents oral medications from staying down, so the rectal route bypasses the upper gastrointestinal tract entirely. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T18#GNS125_U3_T18_h1)

question: Which nerve carries visual signals from the eye to the brain?

options.A: The auditory nerve
options.B: The trigeminal nerve
options.C: The oculomotor nerve
options.D: The optic nerve

explanation: The optic nerve acts like a data cable, carrying all the visual messages from the back of your eye straight to the brain. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T6#GNS211_U4_T6_h5)

question: What is the most common cause of hypothyroidism when iodine is readily available?

options.A: Hashimoto's thyroiditis
options.B: Anterior pituitary tumor
options.C: Dietary iodine deficiency
options.D: Chronic viral infection

explanation: Correct! Hashimoto's is an autoimmune condition where the body's immune system accidentally attacks and wears down the thyroid gland over time. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T10#GNS222_U2_T10_h2)

question: Why should nursing schools include hands-on mini-projects during training?

options.A: It provides free labor for hospital administrative departments
options.B: It stops students from pursuing bedside clinical nursing careers
options.C: It builds confidence and practical skills in carrying out future studies
options.D: It ensures students pass their board exams without studying textbooks

explanation: Exactly! Doing small projects early on takes away the anxiety so you feel like a capable researcher long before you graduate. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T6#GNS217_U2_T6_h6)

question: Why should you NEVER use a patient's room number to verify who they are?

options.A: Doctors change room assignments every single hour
options.B: Room numbers are often painted the same color
options.C: Patients frequently switch rooms or beds
options.D: Hospital charts do not display room numbers

explanation: Beds and rooms change all the time in a busy ward. Location is never a safe way to identify a patient! [learn more](GNS125_U3_T1#GNS125_U3_T1_h5)

question: A patient tells you they are too busy with work and transport to visit the gym. What is your best response as a nurse?

options.A: Tell them that exercise is optional if they take their blood pressure medication
options.B: Advise them to stop working so hard and prioritize leisure time instead
options.C: Suggest simple physical activities that can be built directly into daily chores and routines
options.D: Insist that they must find time for a structured gym membership every evening

explanation: Brilliant! Health advice has to be practical. Recommending things like walking more or active housework fits right into their busy schedules without costing extra money. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T15#GNS313_U3_T15_h7)

question: What is a potential risk if a baby's skull undergoes excessive and very rapid moulding?

options.A: Permanent stunting of head growth after birth
options.B: Tearing of intracranial blood vessels
options.C: Complete blockage of cerebrospinal fluid pathways permanently
options.D: Premature fusion of the facial bones

explanation: While moulding is normal, if the bones shift too violently or fast, those delicate blood vessels inside can rupture. That's why monitoring labour progress is so important! [learn more](GNS121_U6_T11#GNS121_U6_T11_h5)

question: What do we call a colostomy problem where the bowel telescopes out and the stoma becomes way too long?

options.A: Retraction
options.B: Hernia
options.C: Necrosis
options.D: Prolapse

explanation: Correct! A prolapse happens when extra bowel pushes out through the stoma site, making it stick out much further than normal. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T14#GNS212_U1_T14_h6)

question: Which of these is one of the most common causes of nursing malpractice claims?

options.A: Failing to attend annual hospital parties
options.B: Forgetting to log into the electronic health record on time
options.C: Medication administration errors
options.D: Refusing to work mandatory overtime shifts

explanation: Giving the wrong drug, wrong dose, or missing a route can easily harm a patient. This is why our 5 rights of medication administration are drilled into us! [learn more](GST322_U4_T9#GST322_U4_T9_h4)

question: Where should a nurse begin looking for a suitable vein for initial cannulation?

options.A: Most distal areas of the upper extremities
options.B: Delicate veins directly over wrist joint creases
options.C: Large veins located in the lower extremities
options.D: Proximal veins close to the upper shoulder

explanation: Starting low on the hand or forearm preserves higher vein sites for future access if the current line fails. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T4#GNS122_U1_T4_h4)

question: Why should a nurse stay non-judgmental when learning about local food taboos?

options.A: To build trust and encourage community members to share openly
options.B: To ensure the nurse receives financial gifts from the village
options.C: To comply with international laws on cultural preservation
options.D: To prove that modern nursing science is inferior to tradition

explanation: Showing respect stops people from getting defensive. When they trust you, they will talk openly and work with you for better health! [learn more](GNS225_U6_T9#GNS225_U6_T9_h6)

question: What should you check or do first when a patient is brought in with a suspected poisoning?

options.A: Drawing blood for toxicology screening
options.B: Identifying the specific poison
options.C: Administering activated charcoal immediately
options.D: Stabilizing the airway, breathing, and circulation

explanation: Great nursing rule to keep in mind! ABC comes before anything else in an emergency. We have to make sure our patient is breathing and has a steady heartbeat before we worry about testing or finding out what they swallowed. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T6#GNS215_U5_T6_h1)

question: Why do nurses promote local foods during cooking demos instead of imported ones?

options.A: Local health policies legally forbid the use of foreign recipes
options.B: Local ingredients are usually more affordable and accessible to the community
options.C: Imported foods cause immediate illness in all age groups
options.D: Imported foods are always completely devoid of any nutritional value

explanation: Spot on! Good nutrition teaching has to be practical. Using foods that families can easily buy or grow nearby ensures the habit sticks. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T17#GNS214_U1_T17_h5)

question: Which communication style involves hiding anger behind sarcastic remarks and delayed tasks?

options.A: Openly passive
options.B: Strictly assertive
options.C: Passive-aggressive
options.D: Directly aggressive

explanation: Passive-aggressive behavior masks true frustration with indirect actions like sarcasm or stalling. [learn more](GST321_U7_T5#GST321_U7_T5_h2)

question: How do you figure out the true urine output for a patient who has continuous bladder irrigation running?

options.A: Measure only the dark red blood collected in the bag
options.B: Divide the total output volume by the number of hours
options.C: Add the amount of irrigation fluid to the total output
options.D: Subtract total fluid infused from total drainage output

explanation: Simple math: take everything in the drainage bag and minus the irrigation fluid you pumped in. What's left is pure urine from the kidneys! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T23#GNS212_U1_T23_h7)

question: A patient with large fibroids complains of constant pelvic pressure and constipation. Why is she likely constipated?

options.A: Side effects from high estrogen levels
options.B: A complete blockage of the small intestine
options.C: Pressure from the fibroids on the rectum
options.D: Severe inflammation of the uterine lining

explanation: An enlarged uterus and bulky fibroids can press backward against the rectum, making bowel movements difficult. Simple anatomy in action! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T22#GNS216_U5_T22_h4)

question: Why are advance directives so helpful in critical or end-of-life care?

options.A: They guarantee that the patient will recover fully
options.B: They guide medical treatment according to the patient's prior wishes
options.C: They eliminate all paperwork for the hospital staff
options.D: They give the doctor total control over all decisions

explanation: Advance directives let patients make their choices known ahead of time, taking the guesswork out of difficult situations. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T1#GNS221_U4_T1_h8)

question: What are the three golden rules of radiation safety?

options.A: Light, heat, and pressure
options.B: Height, weight, and volume
options.C: Time, distance, and shielding
options.D: Speed, velocity, and mass

explanation: Always remember: spend less time near radiation, step back to create distance, and use lead shielding. Safety first! [learn more](GNS123_U2_T10#GNS123_U2_T10_h2)

question: In a drug trial, why do researchers use 'blinding' (hiding who gets the real drug or a fake sugar pill)?

options.A: To make the computer software run faster
options.B: To prove the theoretical construct is correct
options.C: To make sure everyone drops out at the same time
options.D: To stop people's expectations from messing up the results

explanation: If patients or nurses know who got the real medicine, they might act differently or judge results with bias. Blinding keeps everything fair and honest! [learn more](GNS224_U1_T26#GNS224_U1_T26_h6)

question: What is the primary difference between a standard x-ray and a CT scan?

options.A: A CT scan creates cross-sectional 3D images.
options.B: A standard x-ray uses magnetic resonance.
options.C: A standard x-ray can see deep bone infections.
options.D: A CT scan exposes the patient to less radiation.

explanation: CT scanners use computers and rotating x-ray beams to produce detailed, slice-by-slice views of the body, whereas standard x-rays only show flat, two-dimensional shadows. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T6#GNS222_U1_T6_h1)

question: Why is long-term evaluation so important in Behaviour Change Communication?

options.A: It proves that the nurse worked extra hours without taking a break
options.B: It measures whether actual health practices were sustained over time
options.C: It allows the hospital to increase consultation fees for patients
options.D: It replaces the need for daily clinical nursing assessments

explanation: You nailed it! Real habit changes take time. Long-term checks let you know if the community kept up the healthy lifestyle weeks or months later. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T10#GNS124_U5_T10_h6)

question: How does cognitivism view how our minds handle learning?

options.A: As an emotional center completely separate from memory
options.B: As an active information processor similar to a computer
options.C: As a blank slate that only reacts to external rewards
options.D: As a muscle that only grows through physical exercise

explanation: Think of your brain like a smart computer: it takes in data, processes it, stores it safely, and pulls it back out when you need it on the ward. [learn more](GST321_U8_T1#GST321_U8_T1_h3)

question: Which group of medications is most commonly used to manage severe pain and breathlessness in palliative care?

options.A: Antihypertensives
options.B: Antibiotics
options.C: Anticoagulants
options.D: Opioids

explanation: You nailed it! Opioids are the gold standard for getting severe pain and tough breathing under control so the patient can finally rest comfortably. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T3#GNS321_U4_T3_h3)

question: A post-surgical patient cannot pass urine and you suspect they are retaining urine. What is the best bedside tool to check?

options.A: A leg blood flow Doppler
options.B: A portable bladder ultrasound scanner
options.C: A standard chest X-ray
options.D: A full abdominal CT scan

explanation: A portable bladder scanner is quick, non-invasive, and tells you right away how much urine is trapped in the bladder. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T11#GNS123_U2_T11_h8)

question: Why do adolescent girls need more iron in their diet?

options.A: To balance elevated thyroid hormone levels
options.B: To compensate for menstrual blood loss
options.C: To support rapid brain tissue growth
options.D: To prevent adult-onset bone fractures

explanation: Monthly periods mean losing some iron regularly, so young women need iron-rich foods to stay strong and avoid anemia. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T4#GNS312_U3_T4_h6)

question: How do secondary bone tumors differ from primary bone tumors?

options.A: Secondary tumors originate strictly from bone marrow cells
options.B: Secondary tumors are always benign growths that stop growing early
options.C: Secondary tumors only affect the cartilage and never the hard bone
options.D: Secondary tumors spread to the bone from another organ in the body

explanation: Think of secondary tumors as travellers. They started somewhere else like the breast or prostate and hitchhiked to the bones. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T19#GNS222_U1_T19_h1)

question: A public health nurse hands out mosquito nets to prevent malaria. Which part of the epidemiological triad is this mainly targeting?

options.A: Incubation period
options.B: Agent
options.C: Host genetics
options.D: Environment

explanation: Spot on! Mosquito nets create a physical block between you and the environmental vector, modifying the surrounding environment where disease transmission happens. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T1#GNS313_U1_T1_h3)

question: How does male andropause usually differ from female menopause?

options.A: It involves a slow and gradual decline in hormone levels
options.B: It causes an immediate and complete stop to all sperm production
options.C: It affects every single man at exactly age fifty years
options.D: It occurs during early adolescence rather than late adulthood

explanation: Correct! Unlike the quicker hormone drop in female menopause, men experience a very gradual, slow decrease in hormone levels as they age. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T8#GNS311_U1_T8_h5)

question: What is the physical shape of a DNA molecule?

options.A: A flat square sheet
options.B: A single circle
options.C: A branched tree structure
options.D: A double helix

explanation: DNA naturally twists into a spiral ladder shape referred to as a double helix. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T7#GNS111_U1_T7_h1)

question: Why do many women in Nigeria still resort to unsafe abortions despite strict laws?

options.A: Abortion being completely free in government hospitals
options.B: Desire to experience traditional surgical practices
options.C: Lack of access to safe services and modern contraceptives
options.D: Legal encouragement from local community leaders

explanation: Spot on! When family planning services and safe care are hard to reach, vulnerable women sadly turn to dangerous alternatives. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T023#GNS226_U5_T023_h1)

question: Which infant condition is Bryant's traction typically used to treat?

options.A: Spina bifida complications
options.B: Severe clubfoot deformity
options.C: Fractured clavicle from birth
options.D: Congenital hip dislocation

explanation: Bryant's traction gently lifts both of a baby's legs straight up in the air to help realign a dislocated hip. Nursing pediatrics made simple! [learn more](GNS221_U1_T8#GNS221_U1_T8_h3)

question: How does pulmonary circulation differ from systemic circulation?

options.A: Pulmonary circulation bypasses the right side of the heart
options.B: Pulmonary circulation operates under much lower pressure
options.C: Systemic circulation only carries deoxygenated blood
options.D: Systemic circulation has a shorter pathway than pulmonary

explanation: The pulmonary circuit is a low-pressure pathway because the lungs are close to the heart and offer less resistance than the entire systemic body. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h1)

question: Why do nurses use splints and careful positioning for patients with polio?

options.A: To prevent permanent joint contractures and deformities
options.B: To speed up the regeneration of destroyed spinal motor nerves
options.C: To keep the patient completely immobile during ventilation
options.D: To stimulate blood circulation and stop muscle growth

explanation: You got it! When muscles are paralyzed, they pull unevenly. Proper positioning helps keep the joints safe from permanent stiffness. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T15#GNS313_U2_T15_h4)

question: A patient with a racing heart and frequent fainting is scheduled for an EPS. What is the main goal?

options.A: To permanently cure high blood pressure using catheter pressure sensors
options.B: To locate the exact electrical pathway causing the abnormal heart rhythm
options.C: To check how well the heart valves open and close during exercise
options.D: To widen narrowed coronary arteries with a small balloon

explanation: Spot on! The goal is pure detective work: tracking down the exact electrical short circuit that's making the heart race. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T10#GNS222_U3_T10_h2)

question: Which of these is a bad practice when choosing a nutritional supplement?

options.A: Following the recommended dosage instructions on the bottle
options.B: Ignoring product labels and ingredient lists completely
options.C: Buying products verified by independent quality testing
options.D: Checking with a healthcare provider before starting

explanation: Always read the label! Ignoring it means you might miss allergy warnings, wrong dosages, or hidden ingredients. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T013#GNS227_U7_T013_h6)

question: If an epi curve shows multiple waves spaced out by the exact incubation period of an illness, what kind of outbreak is it?

options.A: Continuous waterborne outbreak
options.B: Point-source foodborne outbreak
options.C: Vector-borne seasonal outbreak
options.D: Propagated person-to-person outbreak

explanation: Those rolling waves mean the disease is passing from one person to another across generations of infection. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T10#GNS313_U1_T10_h5)

question: What is the most critical dietary instruction for a patient newly diagnosed with celiac disease?

options.A: Maintain strict, lifelong elimination of all foods containing gluten
options.B: Avoid dairy products only during acute episodes of abdominal pain
options.C: Increase fiber intake temporarily until bowel villi fully regrow
options.D: Reduce fat intake to prevent steatorrhea during flare-ups

explanation: Celiac disease is a permanent condition requiring complete, lifelong removal of gluten to allow mucosal healing and prevent complications. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T8#GNS213_U3_T8_h8)

question: A patient with advanced dementia cannot speak clearly or rate their discomfort on a numbered scale. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Administer a strong opioid immediately to prevent potential hidden distress
options.B: Document that the patient is currently free from any physical pain
options.C: Wait until the family arrives to ask them if the patient looks uncomfortable
options.D: Use a validated observational behavioral tool to check for signs of discomfort

explanation: When verbal communication fails, nurses must rely on validated behavioral scales that observe body movements, facial expressions, and vocal sounds. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T14#GNS321_U4_T14_h3)

question: What is the main goal of injection safety in nursing?

options.A: To prevent harm to the patient, nurse, and community
options.B: To ensure medications dissolve faster in the bloodstream
options.C: To reduce the financial cost of hospital supplies
options.D: To speed up the delivery of emergency medications

explanation: You got this! Injection safety is all about protecting everyone from accidental injury or infection. Keeping patients, ourselves, and our communities safe always comes first. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T3#GNS122_U4_T3_h1)

question: A patient offers you a costly birthday gift during a home visit. What is the best way to handle this?

options.A: Scold the patient harshly for trying to bribe clinical staff
options.B: Accept the gift quickly before other family members see it
options.C: Accept the gift but promise to bring an expensive present back
options.D: Politely decline the gift while thanking the patient for the kind thought

explanation: You got it! Refusing personal gifts kindly helps you maintain professional boundaries while still showing appreciation for the patient's warm intentions. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T4#GNS324_U2_T4_h3)

question: Which shift scheduling practice best helps reduce fatigue-related nursing errors?

options.A: Implementing sensible roster planning with protected rest periods
options.B: Eliminating handovers entirely to keep nurses at the bedside
options.C: Allowing back-to-back double shifts without mandatory breaks
options.D: Requiring all junior staff to work consecutive night shifts indefinitely

explanation: Correct! Well-designed rosters and actual time to rest give the brain a chance to recover, keeping both you and your patients safe. [learn more](GST319_U5_T7#GST319_U5_T7_h4)

question: What is the main difference in how a research objective and a research question are written?

options.A: A question uses medical jargon, while an objective uses everyday language
options.B: An objective is always a guess, while a question is a proven fact
options.C: An objective is written at the end of the study, while a question is written at the beginning
options.D: An objective is a declarative statement using an action verb, while a question is interrogative

explanation: Remember: an objective makes a statement using an action verb (like 'To determine...'), whereas a question asks something directly with a question mark at the end. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T9#GNS217_U3_T9_h3)

question: What is the correct order for examining a patient's tummy (abdomen)?

options.A: Inspection, auscultation, percussion, palpation
options.B: Palpation, percussion, auscultation, inspection
options.C: Auscultation, inspection, palpation, percussion
options.D: Percussion, palpation, inspection, auscultation

explanation: Always listen (auscultate) before you touch or press! Pressing first can change the natural bowel sounds and mess up your assessment. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T11#GNS213_U3_T11_h3)

question: A postnatal mother comes in with a fever and foul-smelling lochia. What does this usually mean?

options.A: Early return of normal menstruation
options.B: Normal involution of the uterus
options.C: Dehydration from breastfeeding
options.D: Postnatal sepsis or infection

explanation: Bad-smelling lochia combined with a fever is a classic red flag for a uterine infection. You'll want to escalate this quickly for medical treatment! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T022#GNS226_U3_T022_h2)

question: What does Multiple Organ Dysfunction Syndrome (MODS) represent in a patient treated for shock?

options.A: A temporary nervous system shock caused by emotional stress
options.B: An allergic reaction to intravenous fluid administration
options.C: Failure of two or more organ systems due to prolonged lack of perfusion
options.D: The normal recovery phase after successful blood pressure stabilization

explanation: MODS occurs when prolonged cellular starvation causes multiple major organs to break down and stop functioning. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T2#GNS221_U3_T2_h7)

question: Why must you teach patients who just had eye surgery to avoid bending over at the waist?

options.A: Sudden head movements can make the new lens fall out.
options.B: Increased facial blood flow stops antibiotic drops from working.
options.C: Bending over increases pressure inside the eye, which can pop delicate stitches.
options.D: Bending over causes dizziness and increases fall risks.

explanation: Bending your head below your heart spikes the pressure inside your eye, which is the last thing you want when fresh stitches are healing! [learn more](GNS311_U3_T3#GNS311_U3_T3_h7)

question: Which of these actions is an example of environmental source reduction to prevent malaria?

options.A: Taking daily anti-malarial tablets prescribed by a doctor
options.B: Draining stagnant puddles of water around the residential compound
options.C: Treating infected patients with intravenous fluid therapy
options.D: Getting vaccinated against mosquito-borne viral infections

explanation: Spot on! Source reduction is about removing the breeding grounds—like clearing out stagnant water where mosquitoes love to lay eggs. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T76#GNS214_U1_T76_h4)

question: How does a copper IUD mainly prevent pregnancy?

options.A: By releasing high doses of estrogen to stop ovulation
options.B: By swelling the cervix shut so sperm cannot enter
options.C: By physically blocking the Fallopian tubes with wire
options.D: By releasing copper ions that stun and damage sperm cells

explanation: The copper creates an environment that sperm really hate. It damages them and stops them from ever reaching the egg! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T015#GNS226_U6_T015_h2)

question: In basic microbiology, what exactly is an infectious agent?

options.A: A genetic trait passed down from parents
options.B: An environmental toxin found in polluted water
options.C: A vitamin deficiency that harms the immune system
options.D: Any microorganism capable of causing disease

explanation: You've got this! An infectious agent is simply any tiny germ—like a bacterium, virus, or fungus—that can get inside the body and cause illness. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T2#GNS313_U1_T2_h1)

question: What is the main difference between delirium and dementia?

options.A: Delirium is an acute, fluctuating change in mental status
options.B: Dementia can be completely cured with antibiotics
options.C: Dementia causes sudden hallucinations without memory loss
options.D: Delirium develops gradually over several years

explanation: Spot on! Delirium comes on suddenly (often because of an infection or illness) and changes throughout the day. Dementia is a slow, long-term decline in memory and thinking. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T5#GNS321_U3_T5_h4)

question: A patient taking a new blood pressure medication suddenly feels very dizzy and lightheaded when standing up. What is the most appropriate immediate nursing action?

options.A: Tell the patient to run in place to improve blood circulation
options.B: Administer a stimulant medication to raise the blood pressure
options.C: Check the patient's blood pressure and pulse immediately
options.D: Wait until the next scheduled clinic visit to report the finding

explanation: Dizziness after starting a new blood pressure drug points to orthostatic hypotension, requiring a check of vital signs. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T2#GNS215_U5_T2_h6)

question: What is the most effective way to keep pests out of a kitchen?

options.A: Leaving all windows open overnight to allow fresh air circulation
options.B: Sweeping the floor once a week after closing business hours
options.C: Keeping food stored off the floor in sealed containers and sealing entry gaps
options.D: Spraying strong insecticides in the dining area every morning

explanation: Correct! If you block their entry points and hide their food source in tight containers, pests won't bother showing up. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T009#GNS227_U3_T009_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a typical symptom of bacterial food poisoning?

options.A: Sudden bone fracture
options.B: Watery or bloody diarrhea
options.C: Severe abdominal cramps
options.D: Nausea and vomiting

explanation: Foodborne illness hits your gut, causing tummy cramps, vomiting, and diarrhea—it doesn't cause broken bones! [learn more](GNS227_U3_T011#GNS227_U3_T011_h7)

question: What is an important safety action when a patient wants to use herbal supplements in the hospital?

options.A: Encourage the patient to double their dosage for faster healing
options.B: Confiscate all herbal products immediately because they are dangerous
options.C: Ignore what the patient takes as long as they swallow their pills
options.D: Screen the supplements for potential interactions with prescribed medications

explanation: Spot on! Herbal products can react strongly with conventional drugs, so as nurses, we always check for safety interactions first. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T2#GNS123_U1_T2_h5)

question: Why must everyone in a household get treated at the same time if one person has pinworms?

options.A: Untreated relatives will develop severe liver failure within forty-eight hours
options.B: Family members share identical genetic susceptibility to roundworm larvae
options.C: Single treatments are legally prohibited for treating minor household pests
options.D: Pinworms spread rapidly among family members through silent reinfection cycles

question: A nurse is preparing to use a blood pressure cuff on a patient with unbroken skin. How should this item be classified and processed?

question: Why is assessing family dynamics an important first step for a nurse?

question: How does evaluating nursing students help protect the public?

question: Which medication is an opioid antagonist that blocks the effects of alcohol and opioids?

question: What causes sudden mood swings or impulsive behavior in patients with inherited brain degeneration?

question: As a nurse writing notes for a domestic violence survivor, how should you document physical injuries?

question: A patient is worried about using modern contraceptives because of her religion. As a nurse, what is the best way to respond?

question: What causes an endocrine pathology related to receptor dysfunction when hormone levels are normal?

question: How is the Hepatitis A virus mainly spread from person to person?

question: What is the simple definition of a nutrient?

question: Which psychosocial issue is closely linked to a weaker immune system in seniors?

question: Why is watching out for drug safety after a medicine goes on the market so important in Nigeria?

question: Why are audiovisual aids considered very powerful in nursing skills training?

question: Why is the CSSD so important for infection control?

question: Why might a dying patient suddenly become restless, pull at their blankets, or reach into the air?

question: What should a healthy, newly formed intestinal stoma look like when you check it?

question: Why do resource-limited regions often report higher rates of patient harm?

question: What is the medical term for a fever?

question: Why do twin pregnancies so often result in early labour?

question: Why is the spinal epidural space considered a real space, while the cranial epidural space inside the head is just a potential space?

question: What is the main job of a mechanical ventilator in the hospital?

question: Which test gives the definitive, 100% confirmation of CJD?

question: What is considered the single most important measure to prevent healthcare-associated infections?

options.A: Taking daily antibiotics

question: In community health nursing, who is considered your primary client?

question: Which of the following is NOT a common challenge facing DRF exemptions in public hospitals?

question: What is the safest medication choice to control blood sugar in gestational diabetes?

explanation: Insulin is the top choice because it generally doesn't cross over the placenta to the baby, keeping blood sugar managed safely. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T5#GNS215_U6_T5_h4)

question: What happens in the body to make a woman's basal body temperature rise slightly right after ovulation?

question: A student wants to study a rare tropical disease requiring expensive lab kits, but has no funding. Which check is this study failing?

question: What is the oily substance produced by sebaceous glands called?

question: What is the proper way to cut fingernails during routine care?

question: What two main changes happen in the blood during asphyxia?

options.D: Low glucose and high lactic acid

question: A patient who lost the use of their legs angrily snaps at the nurse. How should the nurse see this?

options.C: As a sign that the patient should be immediately discharged from rehab

explanation: Have empathy! Anger is completely normal when someone is mourning the loss of their abilities. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T5#GNS123_U6_T5_h7)

question: How do hookworm larvae usually get into the human body from dirty soil?

question: A patient on metronidazole asks if they can take a small drink of alcohol with dinner. What should you tell them?

question: A patient is prescribed five different medications for chronic illnesses and begins missing doses due to confusion. What is the most likely clinical consequence?

options.A: Automatic resistance to all known classes of surgical anesthetics
options.B: Permanent physical dependence on the prescribed pharmaceutical drugs
options.C: Treatment failure and worsening of the underlying health conditions

question: Why is writing clear and prompt nursing notes after a delivery so important?

question: What happens if a nurse crushes an enteric-coated tablet before giving it to a patient?

question: Which clinical sign helps you tell kwashiorkor apart from marasmus?

question: A 15-year-old visits the clinic with eye strain, a stiff neck, and poor sleep after spending 6 hours on social media every night. What is the best term for this?

question: Which type of underwear helps prevent moisture buildup and lowers the risk of vulvitis?

question: Which physical check is commonly done at the bedside to test for low calcium levels (hypoparathyroidism)?

question: Which gland releases prolactin into the blood to make milk?

question: What is an immediate nursing task to take care of right after an ultrasound scan ends?

question: What age threshold is generally used to define a teenage bride?

question: What is an example of hazard substitution in a healthcare setting?

question: What is the main purpose of delivering a shock with an Automated External Defibrillator (AED)?

question: Why might an adolescent with untreated depression turn to substance abuse?

question: Imagine a nurse is testing a new handwashing technique and makes sure every ward uses the exact same water temperature and soap brand. Why do this?

question: Why is keeping patient information strictly confidential especially vital in post-abortion care?

question: Why must a healthcare plan include flexibility?

question: Why don't large proteins and blood cells normally show up in freshly filtered urine?

question: Which blood tests are most vital for tracking complications in a patient with severe, ongoing watery stools?

question: What does the acronym VCT stand for in HIV nursing care?

question: Which characteristic best describes a transformational leader?

question: What is a major systemic challenge frequently facing primary health care centers in Nigeria today?

question: Eighteen months after losing her husband, a widow still cannot leave her house, eat well, or talk about him without panicking. What kind of grief is she experiencing?

question: Which physical examination technique is rarely used today for routine heart checks?

question: How does endocrine hyposecretion usually show up in a patient over time?

question: What common farming practice greatly increases the spread of Taenia solium in rural areas?

question: Why do nurses do an evaluation at the end of a care plan?

question: Why is simple washing not considered true sterilization?

question: Why is a patient hyperoxygenated right before undergoing tracheobronchial suctioning?

question: Since there is no cure for established paralytic polio, what is the main goal of treatment?

question: What do we mean by 'molecular mimicry' in autoimmune conditions?

question: Why are IEC materials so important in primary health care?

question: What is the primary purpose of performing a skin biopsy in dermatology?

question: Why do past surgeries in the tummy make a new laparoscopy trickier?

question: Why must the skin around the incision be cleansed with an antiseptic before cutting the threads?

options.C: To remove surface bacteria and prevent deep infection
options.D: To stain the thread so it is easier to see

explanation: Cleansing eliminates germs sitting on the skin surface, ensuring they do not enter the tiny tract when the thread is pulled through. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h4)

question: How can a nurse help a patient who gets full too quickly eat more calories without eating huge meals?

options.A: Remove all dairy products from the food tray
options.B: Encourage drinking large volumes of water with meals
options.C: Add healthy fats and oils to everyday foods
options.D: Advise the patient to eat only one large meal a day

explanation: Adding fats concentrates calories into smaller portions, making it much easier for a patient who fills up quickly to get enough energy. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T009#GNS227_U6_T009_h4)

question: What is a vital safety step when nursing a patient with Wernicke encephalopathy?

options.A: Setting up fall precautions because of poor coordination
options.B: Encouraging heavy gym workouts to build leg strength
options.C: Restricting all fluids to stop brain swelling
options.D: Keeping the room pitch black all day

explanation: Spot on! Because these patients struggle with balance (ataxia), keeping them safe from nasty falls is a top nursing priority. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T7#GNS222_U4_T7_h6)

question: Which human sense is widely believed to be the absolute last to fade before a patient dies?

options.A: Hearing
options.B: Touch
options.C: Sight
options.D: Taste

explanation: Hearing usually stays intact longer than other senses. That's why we always encourage families to keep talking and comforting their loved ones right up until the end. Beautiful nursing knowledge! [learn more](GNS221_U4_T4#GNS221_U4_T4_h4)

question: In a research table, what do we call the leftmost column that lists the main categories?

options.A: Title
options.B: Stub
options.C: Boxhead
options.D: Footnote

explanation: Think of the 'stub' as the leftmost column that holds your row labels or main items being measured, like the names of different vital signs. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T6#GNS217_U4_T6_h2)

question: What is the main goal of disease surveillance at the primary health care level?

options.A: To manufacture pharmaceutical drugs for local distribution
options.B: To collect taxes from patients seeking medical treatment
options.C: To detect unusual increases in cases early and report them
options.D: To construct new hospital buildings in rural districts

explanation: Surveillance is like keeping a watchful eye on health patterns so health workers can spot a sudden spike before it becomes a major outbreak. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T88#GNS214_U1_T88_h6)

question: Why is maintaining strict confidentiality regarding family planning crucial in community nursing?

options.A: To prevent the clinic from keeping accurate statistical records
options.B: To ensure that contraceptives are sold at higher market prices
options.C: To protect clients from social stigma and domestic conflict
options.D: To hide the nurse's activities from local government leaders

explanation: Clients may face backlash or relationship issues if their contraceptive choices are shared without permission in tight-knit communities. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T15#GNS324_U3_T15_h8)

question: What is an autoantigen?

options.A: A synthetic chemical manufactured inside a sterile laboratory
options.B: A protein transferred from an animal graft to a human patient
options.C: A normal body tissue mistakenly attacked by the immune system
options.D: A harmful bacterial toxin inhaled directly from the outside air

explanation: 'Auto' means self. An autoantigen happens when the immune system gets confused and mistakenly treats normal body parts like enemies. [learn more](GST114_U4_T2#GST114_U4_T2_h3)

question: What is the name of the natural pacemaker that sets the rhythm for the heart?

options.A: Purkinje fiber
options.B: Bundle of His
options.C: Atrioventricular node
options.D: Sinoatrial node

explanation: The Sinoatrial (SA) node is the boss of heart rhythms! It fires off electrical signals the fastest, keeping the whole heart beating in a steady, regular pattern. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h5)

question: What is the main laboratory test used to detect chlamydia and gonorrhea from a swab or urine sample?

options.A: Nucleic Acid Amplification Tests
options.B: Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay
options.C: Stool occult blood analysis
options.D: Complete blood count with differential

explanation: NAATs are the gold standard! They accurately copy and spot tiny amounts of the germ's genetic material. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h6)

question: Which method is best when teaching a community with low literacy levels?

options.A: Giving long lectures without any visual props or pictures
options.B: Using visual aids, drama, and group demonstrations
options.C: Writing detailed medical prescriptions on the chalkboard
options.D: Distributing dense scientific textbooks to every household

explanation: Correct! Pictures, role-play, and practical demos bypass reading barriers and make health messages fun and easy to grasp. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T10#GNS124_U5_T10_h4)

question: Which environmental issue is a major breeding ground for malaria mosquitoes in local neighborhoods?

options.A: Thick concrete flooring inside residential buildings
options.B: Blocked drainage channels and stagnant water pools
options.C: Dry sandy soil found in northern farming regions
options.D: Solar panels installed on health center roofs

explanation: Mosquitoes love standing water! Blocked drains and puddles give them a safe place to lay eggs, which drives up malaria rates. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T9#GNS122_U3_T9_h2)
